S19.01.note: No separate 'accepted' word; the first sign of work is the 'Thinking…' line.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type any short message and press Enter.
Look at the line just under the transcript: it should read 'Thinking…' with a seconds count, before any answer text appears.
S19.01.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type a message, press Enter. The line under the transcript starts with 'Thinking…' and a seconds count.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Attach a file or mention a file with @ in the message, then press Enter.
Look for 'Preparing context…' under the transcript before the answer starts.
S19.03.where: In Terminal run `agi`, attach a file or add context, then send. The line under the transcript reads 'Preparing context…' before the model answers.

S19.04.needs: a web search key (code says /search needs one)
S19.04.note: The code has no visible word 'Searching'; the state is shown only as a running tool row with the ⌕ icon and its name.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type `/search <a question about a recent topic>` and press Enter.
Look for a tool row with the ⌕ icon and a spinner while the search runs.
S19.04.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type /search followed by a question, press Enter. A tool row with the search icon ⌕ appears while the search runs.

S19.05.needs: none (default permission mode asks for approval)
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type `run the command echo hello` and press Enter.
Press Yes at the approval panel.
Look for the $ tool row with a spinner while the command runs, then a check mark when done.
S19.05.where: In Terminal run `agi`, ask it to run a shell command, then approve. The tool row with the $ icon shows a spinner while the command runs.

S19.06.needs: a connected service (MCP server) set up
S19.06.note: The row shows the tool name, not a separate 'calling service' label.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type `/mcp` and press Enter to see connected services.
Ask the agent to use a tool from one of them and press Enter.
Look for the tool row with the service tool name and a spinner while it runs.
S19.06.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type /mcp to see connected services, then ask the agent to use one. Its tool row shows while it runs.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal (default permission mode).
Type `create a file called test.txt containing hello` and press Enter.
Look for 'Waiting for your approval' under the transcript and the approval panel with buttons.
Press Yes or Deny All and check the turn continues or stops.
S19.07.where: In Terminal run `agi`, ask for an action that needs approval. The turn shows 'Waiting for your approval' with approval buttons.

S19.08.needs: none (the agent decides when to ask)
S19.08.note: Nothing forces the agent to ask; the tester cannot trigger it on demand.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Give a task that is ambiguous so the agent may ask you something.
Look for the 'Question from the agent' panel.
Choose an option with arrow keys and Enter, or type your own answer, and check the turn continues.
S19.08.where: In Terminal run `agi`. When the agent asks a question during a task, a panel titled 'Question from the agent' appears with choices and 'Type your own answer'.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type a short message and press Enter.
Watch the 'Thinking…' line; when the first text arrives it should be replaced by the answer.
S19.09.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type a message, press Enter. The 'Thinking…' line is replaced by the answer text.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Ask for a long answer, for example `explain how a hash map works in detail`, and press Enter.
Watch the answer text grow line by line before the 'Thinking…' line disappears.
S19.10.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type a message, press Enter. The answer text grows on screen while the model is still writing.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Ask `give me a bulleted list, a small table, and a code block`, and press Enter.
Watch the answer while it streams: the list, table and code block should show formatted, not as raw markup.
S19.11.where: In Terminal run `agi`, ask for a list, a table and a code block. They appear formatted while the answer is still streaming.

labels.text: Generating the image. Esc stops it.

S19.13.needs: an AGI account (the image command is for managed accounts)
S19.13.note: The code shows a start line and no progress percentage.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type `/image a red bicycle on a beach` and press Enter.
Look for the line 'Generating the image. Esc stops it.' and a running state while it draws.
Press Esc to stop and check the turn ends.
S19.13.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type /image followed by a prompt and press Enter. The line 'Generating the image. Esc stops it.' appears.

S19.15.note: The label is the format string in the code; the screen shows real numbers.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Type a short message and press Enter.
Wait until the 'Thinking…' line disappears.
Look for the detail line under the answer with model, tokens and duration.
S19.15.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a prompt and let it finish. The spinner stops and the answer line shows model, tokens in and out, and time.

S19.16.needs: a run where some steps fail and others succeed
S19.16.note: Searched apps/cli/src for 'partial', 'Partially' and 'with errors'; no partially-completed label exists. The only related view is the header counts 'N completed · N failed' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs).

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send a prompt that gives a long answer, and press Enter.
While it works, press Esc.
Look for 'stopping the turn…' in the footer until the turn ends.
S19.17.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a long prompt, press Esc while it works. The footer shows 'stopping the turn…'.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send a long prompt and press Enter.
Press Esc once text has started to appear.
Look for '⊘ Stopped' under the transcript and check the partial text is still there.
S19.18.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a long prompt, press Esc. The transcript shows '⊘ Stopped' and keeps the text that already arrived.

S19.20.needs: a session that was still running
S19.20.note: No separate 'resuming' word is shown; the code only shows 'Resumed session'.
steps: Start a long background or long prompt, then close the terminal.
Open Terminal, run `agi resume` and pick the session, or run `agi resume <session id>`.
Look for 'Resumed session … (N messages).' and check the unfinished work is continued, not started from scratch.
S19.20.where: In Terminal run `agi resume <session id>`, or inside `agi` type /resume. The line 'Resumed session … (N messages).' appears.

S19.21.needs: a provider that rate-limits (not on demand)
S19.21.note: Only shown when the provider actually rate-limits; the wait time appears only when the provider gives one.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send prompts until the provider rate-limits (cannot be forced on demand).
Look for the error line in the transcript that gives the wait time or says to wait and retry.
S19.21.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a prompt. When a provider rate-limits, the turn ends with a red error line 'is rate-limiting. Wait …s' or 'Rate limited, retry after …s'.

labels.text: Run `agi usage` to see when it resets.

S19.22.needs: an account that reaches its plan limit
S19.22.note: Upgrade wording comes from a server-side paywall text, not a fixed string.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send prompts until the plan limit is reached (cannot be forced on demand).
Look for the error line with 'It resets in' or the 'agi usage' hint.
Type `/usage` and compare the usage shown.
S19.22.where: In Terminal run `agi`, type /usage to see usage. A turn blocked by a plan limit shows 'It resets in …' or 'Run `agi usage` to see when it resets.'

labels.text: Run `agi login` to sign in to your AGI account again.

S19.23.note: The code gives a text hint to run `agi login`; no in-panel sign-in button for this error was found, so 'offers to sign in' may not match.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal with an expired sign-in.
Send a prompt.
Look for the error line that says to run `agi login` to sign in again.
Run `agi login` and check the next prompt works.
S19.23.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a prompt after sign-in has expired. The error line says 'Run `agi login` to sign in to your AGI account again.'

labels.text: Pick another model with `agi models list`, or try again later.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send a prompt while the provider is unavailable (cannot be forced on demand).
Look for the error line with 'Retry the request' or 'Pick another model'.
Type `/model` and pick another model, then send again.
S19.25.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a prompt while the provider is down. The error line says '…returned HTTP …' and suggests a retry or another model.

steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Paste a very long text as the prompt and press Enter.
Look for the error line 'Context exceeded for' with the `/compact` tip.
Type `/compact`, then send the message again.
S19.26.where: In Terminal run `agi`, send a prompt that is too long. The error line says 'Context exceeded for …' and suggests `/compact`.

labels.text: The connection closed before the answer finished.

S19.27.note: The partial text is kept by the code path that commits turn entries before the error line.
steps: Run `agi` in Terminal.
Send a long prompt and let the connection drop (cannot be forced on demand).
Look for the partial answer still on screen, then the error line 'The connection closed before the answer finished.'
S19.27.where: In Terminal run `agi`. If the stream breaks after text arrived, the kept text stays and the error line says 'The connection closed before the answer finished.'

S19.28.note: Unsure whether the '⊘ Stopped' marker itself is saved and comes back; the code adds it to the chat only.
steps: Send a prompt, let it finish, then quit `agi`.
Run `agi resume` in Terminal and pick the session.
Look for 'Resumed session … (N messages).' and check the earlier turns are shown as before.
S19.28.where: Quit `agi`, then in Terminal run `agi resume` and pick the session, or inside `agi` type /resume. The earlier conversation and turns come back.

steps: Run `agi background start write a short summary of this folder`.
Close the Terminal window.
Open a new Terminal and run `agi background list`; check the state label.
Run `agi background attach <id>` when it says finished, and check the result is there.
S19.29.where: In Terminal run `agi background start <prompt>` (alias `agi bg start`), then `agi background list`. Use `agi background attach <id>` when it is done.
